opus.why: Checks one still against a written brief and checklist, with JSON output. Spotting anatomy and palette errors needs careful vision, but the scope is tight and the laws are explicit.

fable.why: Scoped single-image judgment with a written brief and checklist; needs reliable vision on anatomy/wheel/palette details, which Sonnet handles and Haiku misses on fine defects.

opus.why: Visual QA on 8 renders to decide what goes in the carousel. Subtle defects (merged limbs, missing wheels, fused helmets) need the stronger vision model so none slip through.

fable.why: Eight images to inspect for subtle anatomy defects and a keep/discard call for a published carousel; visual judgment matters, Sonnet's vision is sufficient, Haiku is not reliable on merged limbs and missing parts.

opus.why: Comparing three short captions where the brief is clear and the winner is fairly obvious. Sonnet makes the copy-taste call well.

fable.why: Three short captions, one is obviously weak; picking the winner and naming what to borrow is routine copy judgment Sonnet does well without extra effort.

opus.why: Critiquing a 60s script. The problems are visible (weak hook, too much VO, generic outro), and pacing advice and cut suggestions fit Sonnet well.

fable.why: Script critique needs pacing sense (words per second vs timing), hook judgment and concrete cut points in Russian; Sonnet at high gives the editorial care, Haiku tends to be generic.

opus.why: Pitch deck QC from an investor's view. The issues are findable (40 vs 30 min, Mara's name duplicated, 'no competitors', internal TAM, tense mix). Investor framing gains from high effort.

fable.why: Deck QC requires catching every inconsistency (duplicate team name, 40 vs 30 min, tense, 'no competitors', internal-estimate TAM) and thinking like an investor; thoroughness needs high effort but not Opus.

opus.why: Honest critique of five LinkedIn posts already in context and picking two to cut. This is copy judgment on public-facing content, but analysis only.

fable.why: Honest self-critique of LinkedIn copy and a drop-two decision; copy judgment where the owner acts on the ranking, so Sonnet high rather than Haiku.

opus.why: Finding contradictions in a brand book. They're fairly overt (exclamation-mark example, Ember packaging vs the 10% rule, vague logo rules), and the user wants a short list.

fable.why: Contradictions in the brand book are concrete and findable (exclamation example, Ember 10% vs packaging, white seamless vs natural light, vague logo rules); short list output, Sonnet medium catches them.

opus.why: Deciding whether a judge's hand-anatomy fail was real or false. Needs close visual re-inspection and reasoning about where the judge went wrong, and that settles trust in the pipeline.

fable.why: Adjudicating a disputed hand-anatomy fail on a crop sheet needs the strongest vision and careful reasoning about the prior judge's error; a wrong call either ships a defect or discards good work.

opus.why: One-line pick between two thumbnail titles. It's a quick taste call, but audience-facing, so Sonnet at low effort rather than Haiku.

fable.why: One-line pick between two thumbnail titles; a clear curiosity-vs-claim comparison Haiku answers correctly.
